rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: glucose 11.1 or more with danger signs / Check for urgent signs when fingerprick glucose is 11.1 or more
rule_level_problems.problem: Footnote 7 defines 'Dehydration' as thirst, dry mouth, poor skin turgor, BP < 90/60, pulse >= 100. Only the bare disorder concept is used. The two vital-sign components are routine measurements the system already holds (Systolic/Diastolic blood pressure, Heart rate; all exist as observable entities) and the three findings have concepts (Excessive thirst, Xerostomia, Decreased skin turgor). The gold standard expands such footnote definitions (page 20 writes BP < 90/60 as two measurements). Suggested: add an (or (clinical_finding Dehydration) (< SBP 90) (< DBP 60) (>= Heart rate 100) ...) group to the priority rule and the findings to the check_for.

rule_level_problems.problem: The page's 'Diagnose diabetes' box adds 'If < 35 years, type 1 diabetes likely. Refer.' The grammar has no numeric age comparison (only adult / older child / younger child), so a probable 'Diabetes mellitus type 1' rule cannot be written. The whole fasting-glucose pathway (6.1-11 branch, risk-factor screen, 6.1-6.9 = impaired fasting glucose, >= 7 twice = diabetes) is likewise unrepresentable because the release has no fasting-glucose observable entity. None of this is a builder error, but the file gives no sign these were weighed; they belong in a 'could not model' note so the omission is not mistaken for a miss.

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for symptoms of diabetes when glucose is 11.1 or more without ketones
rule_level_problems.problem: The due_to uses (no Ketonuria) and (no known Diabetes mellitus). Both are answered by tasks that fire on the same >= 11.1 trigger, so the gate works; but if 'no' means 'recorded as absent' rather than 'not recorded', a patient whose ketone result is never entered is never asked about symptoms and the probable-diabetes rule can never fire for them. The ordering is correct per the page; flagging only so the semantics of 'no' are confirmed.

summary: The red-box logic of both triage boxes is encoded correctly: hypoglycaemia (< 3, or < 4 with known diabetes) as a probable diagnosis driving an Urgent priority, and glucose >= 11.1 with any of the ten listed danger signs, or with urine ketones, as Urgent, with every sign mapped to a concept that exists and means what the page says (Confusion -> Clouded consciousness, Rapid deep breathing -> Kussmaul's respiration). The one substantive gap is 'Dehydration', whose footnote definition (BP < 90/60, pulse >= 100, thirst, dry mouth, poor skin turgor) is collapsed into a single disorder concept even though its vital-sign parts are routine measurements, so a hyperglycaemic patient with SBP 85 and pulse 110 is not flagged unless 'Dehydration' is recorded by hand. The remaining omissions (type 1 diabetes likely under 35, the whole fasting-glucose work-up and its risk-factor screen) are language limits, not builder errors, but nothing in the file shows they were considered.
